items.rationale: The in-car impact is covered under §§2.6.2 and 4.5.2, and the battery health waiver prevents exclusion under §2.6.8. The supplier’s uneconomic-repair report supports replacement under §§7.1.9–7.1.10: estimated at €850 gross for an equivalent new unit less €50 estimated salvage, with no stated deductible or sub-limit to apply.
Section 7.1.9 limits payment to the equivalent pre-loss specification, already allowed on line 1. The separately billed elective upgrade has no covered share.
The cracked screen is covered impact damage under §§2.6.2–2.6.4. Allow €185 gross for a comparable screen fitted and tested under §§7.1.7 and 7.1.10, with no separate deductible for the tablet.

Section 5.2.3 covers necessary diagnostics for both units, including the laptop deemed uneconomic to repair. Allow €40 per device, or €80 gross against the shared €250 event cap, assuming no diagnostic charge was credited elsewhere.
Under §§4.2.6 and 7.1.5, a carrying case is assessed separately and must itself have been damaged. The undamaged bag has no covered replacement cost.
Sections 3.5(f) and 7.1.8(e) exclude the cost of future warranty protection, even when purchased with a covered replacement.
Sections 3.5(d) and 4.3(c) exclude data recovery unless separately endorsed, and no such endorsement is stated. Physical damage to the laptop does not make file extraction payable.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes separately billed administrative charges, and the underlying data recovery is itself excluded under §3.5(d).
